links.claim: QBiC-SELEX predicts stronger in-vitro binding to alt using an ETV5-mapped ETS model shared by related factors. GABPA is expressed and has variant-overlapping peaks only in other biosamples; no peak was found in U-87 MG, so GABPA-specific occupancy in this glioblastoma model is unestablished.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE with active-chromatin marks, but the reported marks are maxima across biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific measurements.

TERT is the nearest annotated TSS, but neither proximity nor the absence of a significant brain-cortex eQTL demonstrates that this cCRE regulates TERT; the literature search returned no variant-specific functional result.
GABPA is expressed in the stated glioblastoma context, but there is no matching-context ChIP peak at the variant, including in U-87 MG.

TERT promoter alterations are relevant background in glioblastoma and melanoma, but the evidence does not link this variant or GABPA binding to a disease phenotype and provides no specific support for bladder cancer.

predictions: In an active glioblastoma model carrying both alleles, GABPA occupancy should be greater on alt than ref if GABPA is responsible for the ETS-family in-vitro signal.
If the variant has a regulatory effect through GABPA, that effect should be reduced by GABPA depletion; the direction of any TERT-expression change is not established.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-resolved assay in an active, relevant model finds no greater GABPA occupancy on alt than ref.
Precise editing produces no reproducible GABPA-dependent regulatory effect in a model where the element is active.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.

Conclusions: Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
The genetic landscape of familial melanoma is heterogeneous.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
Mutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

The rs[masked] C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
The prognostic relevance of CDKN2A deletion may vary according to TERTp status, particularly for OS.
